run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T05:47:17Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy reflects a short burst of real HTTP 500 responses. frontend-proxy's own access log matched 69 lines of "POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream in the 05:37:00-05:41:30Z interval, with the burst ending by 05:39:26.9Z (evidence 2ed8e9a5-9c84-4172-88c4-71b8d82a80ae-t0:4d747666-15e7-4d2b-baff-5cd745f2b4db). Those failures trace to checkout's client spans for oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, whose error counter rose from 28 at 05:38:45Z to a final 69 at 05:39:45Z (evidence b46135f1-eded-41f9-8477-8baf1b399a9c-t0:a2260c2b-1489-4787-82b2-2724db1ab96d), and it stopped precisely when the payment Deployment's rollout restart (annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:37:39Z on the new ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786, same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment as the old one) replaced the only payment pod; the new payment container logged "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" only at 2026-11-17T05:38:57.571Z, so no payment server was listening for roughly 75 s after the old pod was killed at 05:37:42Z. Payment's application was not itself erroring: every charge it received during and after the burst is logged "Charge request received." followed by "Transaction complete.", and its charge spans carry no ERROR status. The alert timestamp (05:47:17Z) is after the burst had already stopped, and the RequestErrorRate rule itself could not be read, so the alert's 0.0222 value and evaluation window are unverified. A flagd fault-injection setting paymentUnreachable="on" exists in the flagd-config ConfigMap, but it is not established as the cause (see hypothesis/counter-evidence) and the payment Deployment rollout is the object whose change produced the observed failures.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own access log recorded 69 lines of POST /api/checkout returning HTTP 500 ("500 - via_upstream") inside the queried 2026-11-17T05:37:00Z-05:41:30Z window; the newest 25 shown run from 05:38:56.602Z to 05:39:26.874Z and 44 earlier matched lines in the window were not shown, so the burst began at or after 05:37:00Z and ended by 05:39:27Z.

frontend-proxy's ingress span error rate deviated from its background level (0-8 errors per 1-minute bucket between 05:21 and 05:38) to 58 in the 05:39 bucket and 80 in the 05:40 bucket, then back to 2 at 05:41; the metric timestamps appear lagged relative to the proxy log event times.

checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) accumulated 28 errors by 05:38:45Z and 69 errors by 05:39:45Z, then stayed at 69 for the rest of the query window - a bounded burst of 69 failed charge calls.

Error spans in this incident are the checkout path only: checkout shows STATUS_CODE_ERROR on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge; frontend shows STATUS_CODE_ERROR on POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder; frontend-proxy shows STATUS_CODE_ERROR on ingress and router frontend egress.

The payment Deployment was rolled out at 05:37:39Z: new ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:37:39Z while its container image is unchanged (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, identical to previous ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9, which is now scaled to 0).

Kubernetes events attribute the change to Deployment payment: ScalingReplicaSet at 05:37:39Z (scale up payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1) and 05:37:42Z (scale down payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0), with Pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started 05:37:39-05:37:42Z and old Pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 Killing at 05:37:42Z.

The replacement payment container logged "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" at 2026-11-17T05:38:57.571Z, i.e. about 75 s after the old payment pod was killed at 05:37:42Z, which is the interval in which checkout's charge calls failed.

Payment's application was not erroring: its logs show each received charge as "Charge request received." immediately followed by "Transaction complete." from 05:40:24Z-05:41:29Z and again 05:44:08Z-05:44:59Z, and its charge span series carries only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no ERROR series for span_name charge).

Current cluster state is consistent with recovery: Deployment payment (generation 2, observedGeneration 2) is 1/1 ready, only payment and flagd have generation 2, all otel-demo deployments report 1 available replica, and Service payment resolves to the single endpoint pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo contains fault-injection flags, including paymentUnreachable with defaultVariant "on" (description "Payment service is unavailable") and paymentFailure with defaultVariant "off".

The flagd Deployment starts with "--uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json" and the flagd container mounts only the emptyDir volume config-rw at /etc/flagd; the flagd-config ConfigMap is mounted as a separate volume (config-ro) that the flagd container does not mount, and the running flagd pod (ReplicaSet flagd-678dcfdc67) was created at 05:07:21Z, i.e. it serves a start-up copy of the flags file rather than live ConfigMap edits.

The flagd-config fault setting paymentUnreachable="on" is a candidate cause because its declared fault ("Payment service is unavailable") matches the observed checkout->payment failure path, but it is not established: checkout charges succeed now while the ConfigMap still shows "on", flagd serves a copy of the flags file taken at its 05:07:21Z start, and the observed failure window is only ~100 s long, which a static boolean flag does not explain.

Against the paymentUnreachable-flag explanation: the error burst stopped by 05:39:27Z and checkout charges succeed afterwards (payment logs show completed transactions and payment is 1/1 ready) while the flagd-config ConfigMap still declares paymentUnreachable defaultVariant "on" at query time; a flag being served as "on" would not produce a self-limiting ~100 s burst.

Rejected: that the failing charges were declined inside the payment application itself. Payment's logs show "Transaction complete." for the charges it received and its charge spans carry no ERROR status, so the failures occurred before/without a served charge, matching the ~75 s gap before the new container's gRPC server started rather than an application-level decline.

Determine what issued the payment Deployment rollout restart at 2026-11-17T05:37:39Z (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation, Deployment payment generation 2) using audit/change history, since the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

Make the single-replica payment rollout non-disruptive (startup/readiness probe aligned with the ~75 s gRPC start time, preStop drain, multiple replicas or a PodDisruptionBudget) so a restart does not create a no-endpoint window for checkout's charge calls.

Review the flagd fault configuration: flagd-config still declares paymentUnreachable="on" while the running flagd pod (created 05:07:21Z) serves a start-up copy of the flags file, so this value is dormant until flagd restarts - confirm the intended variant and reload flagd if the setting should take effect or be reverted.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data, so the rule expression, its evaluation window and the reported current value 0.02222222222222222 are unverified, and I cannot explain why the alert fired at 05:47:17Z after the error burst had stopped at ~05:39:27Z.
The change_history integration is not available, so who or what triggered the payment Deployment rollout restart (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:37:39Z) is unknown.

Jaeger returned no traces for checkout or frontend-proxy in the 05:38-05:50Z interval, so the exact span error message/status detail (e.g. gRPC connection-refused text) for the 69 failing charge calls is unknown; the unreachability is inferred from the payment server start time and the timing of the burst, not read from an error message.

The old payment container's logs are unavailable (previous instance not found for pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d and the deleted pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 is gone), so its shutdown behaviour during 05:37:42-05:38:57Z cannot be verified.

flagd's actually served flag values and its logs could not be read (fetch_pod_logs on flagd-678dcfdc67-bl78w returned nothing), so whether checkout ever received paymentUnreachable=true cannot be verified, and the time at which the flagd-config paymentUnreachable value was last changed is unknown.

checkout and frontend application error lines for these failed checkouts were not found (checkout log filter err|error|fail|unreachable|panic|unavailable returned nothing; frontend container logs read 0 bytes), so the application-side error text and frontend-side exception detail remain unverified.
Queries for NetworkPolicy and ResourceQuota objects in otel-demo returned no objects, so their state during the incident is unknown rather than confirmed absent.

The alert window's beginning could not be examined earlier than 05:21Z for per-minute granularity (metric series started 05:17-05:18Z), and the environment's pods were all created at 05:05Z, so behaviour before 05:17Z is unknown.
next_steps: Correlate the payment Deployment rollout restart at 2026-11-17T05:37:39Z with cluster audit logs / CI-CD or operator change records to identify the initiator.
Add a startup/readiness probe and drain behaviour check for the payment gRPC server (~75 s start-up to listening) and consider running payment with more than one replica.
Confirm with the platform owner whether paymentUnreachable="on" in flagd-config is intended; if not, revert it and restart flagd so the running configuration matches the ConfigMap.
If the alert must not fire on such short bursts, review the RequestErrorRate rule's window and threshold (rule definition was not retrievable in this Run).

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
